title: Adding previous-year flow did not clearly lower annual TN:TP error for combined Gulf river loads in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether previous-year river flow improves annual total nitrogen to total phosphorus load ratio estimates for the combined Mississippi and Atchafalaya rivers. We used USGS release 3.0, May 2026, with earlier-year fits and 26 test years in 2000-2025. The baseline used time and current annual flow. Adding log previous-year flow raised squared log error by 2.34%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -19.91% to +10.04%. All planned alternatives also had intervals that included zero. Thus the test did not show a clear accuracy gain, but useful improvement remains possible. Annual loads are model estimates, the test period is short, and the intervals exclude source load and refitting uncertainty. This is annual reconstruction using observed flow, not a lead forecast or a test of a physical storage mechanism. We provide annual aggregate inputs, source hashes, code, all estimates and resampling draws, a figure, and separate arithmetic and direct-source checks.

display.caption: Annual combined TN:TP mass ratio and error reductions from previous-year flow. Intervals are conditional 95% three-year block intervals for fixed held-out losses in 2000-2025.
